Sometimes, Somfy servers don't return any devices. A previous fix handle this by raising an UpdateFailed. But doing this, all devices are marked as unavailable. Because of this, end user cannot move their devices anymore.
Instead of this, now I'm assuming the previous states are still valid.

Hello,
I have the same issue (I've used the beta a few days ago hoping the fix to #44423 would make things better but I had no luck on my side). 
From what I see in the code, I have two suggestions:
1. At https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/d270f9515be39abf7c1989c90956a5c78ed384d2/homeassistant/components/somfy/__init__.py#L99 wouldn't it be better to return the `previous_devices` instead of raising an exception, at least until Somfy fixes the API on their side?
2. The scan interval of 1 minute is perhaps too short, would it be possible to make it configurable (on my part an update per hour would be probably enough for my use cases)?

Anyway thanks for the good work @tetienne!

@efouret when raising UpdateFailed, I already keep the previous devices. `data[COORDINATOR].data` is not deleted. Do you still see unavailable state? 

About the scan interval, we discussed about it [here](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/41352#issuecomment-757532828).  And if you have only RTS devices, we update it to 1 hour. Somfy is OK with this behavior. It’s only 1 request.

@michalkujawa in the mean-time you could use https://github.com/imicknl/ha-tahoma, which makes use of the tahomalink.com server. Currently this is a custom component, but there is an open PR to get it back in Home Assistant as well. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/43966

I am still waiting on the day that Somfy will extend their official API with all device support. And hopefully they will monitor their API and make sure it doesn't fail as often as it does now. It is quite unreliable in automations at the moment, where the Somfy TaHoma integration doesn't have those issues.

@tetienne after looking further into the homeassistant code I'm still wondering if the issue couldn't be caused by the exception raised:
- In https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/4e71be852af8b42a3f43c8da79df4bb956439a80/homeassistant/helpers/update_coordinator.py#L164 when an `UpdateFailed` exception is caught, the `last_update_success` property is set to `False`. 
- And in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/4e71be852af8b42a3f43c8da79df4bb956439a80/homeassistant/helpers/update_coordinator.py#L231 the entity is considered unavailable if `last_update_success` property is `False`.

I'm not sure my analysis is correct but that would explain the behavior.
@efouret thx you very much for the explanation. It can explain indeed the behavior you met. Now I have to think about a nice fix.

review_comments: Should we fail ever the server is flakey for 10x?

If we fail, it means the devices will become unavailable and it will break any automation. Despite the empty response, the server accepts command. 
This error occurs really often. 5 times (5 min) is common.

Will the user still know if the api is down?

If the somfy api goes offline or times out, will the underlying library raise an exception?

The underlying is based on requests, so yes if there is a timeout, or the status is not 200, an exception will be raised.
See https://github.com/tetienne/somfy-open-api/blob/master/pymfy/api/somfy_api.py#L58
Looks like https://github.com/tetienne/somfy-open-api/blob/master/pymfy/api/somfy_api.py#L71 will raise if we get back invalid json.  I think that will raise on a timeout as well
